learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the biosphere, the interconnected web of ecosystems, and the vital importance of preserving the Earth's biodiversity!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The narrow zone of contact between land (lithosphere), water (hydrosphere), and air (atmosphere) where all life forms exist.

A system formed by the interaction of all living organisms (plants, animals) with each other and with their physical environment (sun, soil, water). Examples: a forest, a desert, or even a small pond.
Energy flows from the sun to producers (plants), then to primary consumers (herbivores), and finally to secondary consumers (carnivores). A network of many connected food chains makes a Food Web.
The huge variety of plant and animal life in the world. High biodiversity makes ecosystems stronger and more resilient to disasters.

Human activities like deforestation, pollution, and hunting disrupt ecological balance, leading to the extinction of species. Conservation efforts (like National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries) are necessary to protect life.

fun_activity.title: 🕸️ Build a Food Web
fun_activity.instructions: Write down: Grass, Grasshopper, Frog, Snake, Eagle, and Hawk. Draw arrows showing 'who eats whom'. Notice how they all connect into a complex web rather than a straight line!

exam_tips: 📌 Always define the 'Biosphere' as the intersection of the lithosphere, hydrosphere, and atmosphere.
📌 Differentiate between a Food Chain (a single path of energy) and a Food Web (many interconnected paths).
📌 Be ready to discuss the consequences of disrupting an ecosystem (e.g., if you kill all the frogs, the insect population will explode and destroy crops).
quick_recap: ⭐ The sun is the ultimate source of energy for almost all ecosystems.
⭐ Decomposers (bacteria and fungi) play a crucial role by breaking down dead matter and returning nutrients to the soil.
⭐ Sustainable development means using resources carefully today so they are still available for future generations.
